id_and_class.summary: Keith Frankish holds that conscious experiences are real but not what they seem: the irreducibly subjective ‘phenomenal properties’ or qualia we ascribe to them are an introspective illusion. Introspection builds a simplified, schematic model of the brain’s complex reactions to stimulation, and we mistake that model for direct awareness of inner qualities, so the hard problem gives way to an ‘illusion problem’.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Phenomenal Consciousness as an Introspective Illusion

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Conscious states are complex functional states of the brain that sustain rich sensory engagement with the world and flexible control of behavior. Their distinctive features are functional, which Frankish calls quasi-phenomenal properties.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Conscious experiences are physically realized functional states. Phenomenal properties are intentional objects, represented but never instantiated, like the impossible objects Nicholas Humphrey compares them to.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (consciousness is a functional state of the brain; phenomenality itself is not emergent but illusory)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Conscious states are subjective in a psychological sense: they express an organism’s individual ‘take’ on current stimulation, the cluster of effects it has on that organism. They are not irreducibly subjective, accessible only from the inside.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia do not exist. Introspection misrepresents brain states, as perception misrepresents some features of the world, and introspective information bound to perception makes external things seem to carry vivid sensory qualities, such as an apple’s redness, that reflect their significance for us.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Brains, functional and reactive states, and physically realized representations, including introspective representations that misdescribe experience.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through third-person science of the reactive states that make up a creature’s take on the world. Introspective conviction is a psychological fact to be explained, not epistemic bedrock.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Sensory stimulation triggers reactive changes (attentional, cognitive, conative, affective), which introspection summarizes in a ‘reactivity schema’.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (explained as illusion); Introspection; Sensory experience; Moral status
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The reactivity schema: introspective systems track the overall psychological impact of stimulation without representing its detail, and this simplified model is mistaken for direct acquaintance with qualities. Frankish borrows Daniel Dennett’s image of a computer’s user illusion, whose icons have no literal counterparts in the machine.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Distributed across the brain. The subject of the illusion is the whole organism, and the work of registering and reacting to it is shared among many unconscious subsystems, with no Cartesian theater.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conscious states guide flexible, intelligent behavior. The illusion itself is made of physical representations and so has causal effects, which may be adaptive, as Nicholas Humphrey argues; this avoids the threat of epiphenomenalism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Introspective information is bound to perceptual representations, which makes the illusion ‘outward-looking’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Introspection monitors reactive changes and produces schematic representations useful for communication and high-level self-control but deceptive about their own nature.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Our beliefs about our minds come from evolved biological mechanisms, so they may mislead. The illusion of phenomenality may itself be adaptive.
core_claims_and_evidence: Debunking argument: if belief in phenomenal consciousness can be fully explained by neural processes without reference to phenomenal properties, the belief gives no evidence for them.
Economy: when something resists scientific explanation and is observable from only one perspective, the simplest hypothesis is that it is an illusion.
Weak (‘diet’) illusionism is unstable; it either collapses into strong illusionism or inflates into phenomenal realism.
The appearance-reality objection begs the question, because seeming can be misrepresentation rather than acquaintance.
Pain is bad because it is a complex of strongly aversive states, not because of an ‘intrinsic phenomenal nastiness’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical (debunking and parsimony arguments), informed by cognitive science.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Frankish holds that the reactive changes constituting experience are in principle experimentally detectable, which opens the experiences of other creatures to study.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The central objection, a version of Descartes’ cogito, holds that our own phenomenal states are indubitable data. Galen Strawson argues that illusionism denies the main source of ethical value. Others object that an illusion needs an audience.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Frankish presents illusionism as a broad framework; the exact pattern of introspective distortion can be developed in several ways and is still being worked out.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with physicalism and causal closure, and it avoids the need for radical revisions to the scientific worldview.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness is a complex functional state, a system with the right reactive and sensory organization could have it, though Frankish does not address machines directly.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since conscious states are functional states of a living brain, they end when the brain stops functioning.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Frankish grounds value in what creatures are motivated to seek or avoid and argues that illusionism widens ethical concern to other animals across a graded ‘consciousness space’.
